title: PRISM: Prompt-Refined In-Context System Modelling for Financial Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2511.14130v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Deploying LLMs for financial information retrieval demands accuracy, cost efficiency, and reproducibility, yet most approaches require expensive fine-tuning. PRISM is a training-free framework that composes three deployable modules (prompt engineering, in-context learning, and a candidate refinement module) with a boundary-condition study of multi-agent coordination for financial document retrieval. On FiQA-2018, stacked reranking and $k$-reciprocal encoding raise Recall@100 from 0.7783 to 0.8326. On FinAgentBench, a Cohere-refined top-50 pool yields a higher observed end-to-end NDCG@5, below this evaluation's minimum detectable effect, while cutting per-query cost by about 35%. Added complexity does not always pay off: $k$-reciprocal encoding stops helping once the upstream stage is already high-recall, and multi-agent coordination is not a default for fine-grained chunk ranking. translated_title: PRISM：面向金融检索的提示精炼式上下文系统建模
translated_abstract: 将大语言模型（LLM）部署于金融信息检索需要准确性、成本效率和可复现性，然而大多数方法都需要代价高昂的微调。PRISM 是一个无需训练的框架，它由三个可部署的模块（提示工程、上下文学习和候选精炼模块）组合而成，并针对金融文档检索中的多智能体协作进行了边界条件研究。在 FiQA-2018 数据集上，堆叠式重排序与 k-倒数编码将 Recall@100 从 0.7783 提升至 0.8326。在 FinAgentBench 上，经 Cohere 精炼的 top-50 候选池带来了更高的观测端到端 NDCG@5（低于该评估设置下的最小可检测效应），同时将每条查询的成本削减约 35%。额外增加的复杂性并不总是划算的：当上游阶段已达到高召回率时，k-倒数编码便不再带来增益；而对于细粒度的文本块排序，多智能体协作也并非默认的最优选择。在保持提示、模型和示例一致的配对对比实验中……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: PRISM 提出一种无需训练的金融文档检索框架，通过组合提示工程、上下文学习与候选精炼三个可部署模块，将 FiQA-2018 的 Recall@100 从 0.7783 提升至 0.8326 并降低约 35% 的每查询成本，同时系统性地揭示了 k-倒数编码与多智能体协作等额外复杂性何时不再带来收益的边界条件。
en_tdlr: PRISM is a training-free framework that composes prompt engineering, in-context learning, and candidate refinement modules for financial document retrieval—raising Recall@100 from 0.7783 to 0.8326 on FiQA-2018 while cutting per-query cost by ~35%—and delineates the boundary conditions under which added complexity, such as k-reciprocal encoding and multi-agent coordination, no longer pays off.
